failure_mode: Poor joints: balled or excess solder, lifted pads, intermittent contact
effect: Intermittent SPI errors; corrupted or inconsistent SRAM reads
cause: Hand soldering; heavy solder on the pins
controls: Visual look; data errors show up in captures
evidence: bottom-side photo of the assembled board: balled joints, burnt flux residue
action: Fit sockets and headers in a fixed order; use less solder; clean flux; inspect under magnification; add the steps to an assembly note

effect: Latent damage to the MOSFET or an SRAM chip; odd behaviour later
cause: CMOS parts handled without ESD precautions
evidence: general handling risk for CMOS parts; nothing on this board shows it
action: Handle on an earthed mat or with a wrist strap; keep chips in the sockets only for runs

effect: Switch stuck on or gate swamped: the SRAM never loses power, so captures return retained data and are invalid
cause: 1.27 mm pad pitch leaves a 0.22 mm copper gap; excess solder
controls: Continuity check of the legs; a smoke test of the SRAM supply during a capture
evidence: Aug 2026: all three Q1 legs beeped to each other and the SRAM supply did not drop in the smoke test; the bridge was reworked
action: Change the Q1 footprint (DFM item 1); continuity-check the legs after soldering and before first power

failure_mode: SRAM chip fitted backwards in its socket
effect: Supply applied the wrong way round; chip destroyed or silent
cause: A DIP chip can be inserted either way round
controls: Notch on the socket and on the silkscreen outline
evidence: general risk with DIP sockets; no event recorded
action: Check the notch against pin 1 before first power; add a pin-1 mark on the silkscreen

failure_mode: R2 not fitted: Q1's gate floats while the host pin is not driving it
effect: During host reset or boot the SRAM supply state is undefined; a capture can be spoiled
cause: Pull-down left off; the reason is not recorded (builder does not remember)
evidence: schematic nets: R2 joins the gate net to GND; photo: R2 pads empty
action: Decide: fit R2 or document why not; probe the gate across a host reset with an oscilloscope

failure_mode: Power-up behaviour differs between host boards
effect: The SRAM start-up pattern changes with the host: the same chip gave a different pattern on another host board
cause: Supply rejection of the host regulator, SPI drive strength and ground-plane geometry differ between hosts
controls: Silkscreen 'ONE HOST ONLY'; the 2 x 2 testbed separates host from chip
evidence: thesis D1: same chip on a different host gave a 13.94% intra-device Hamming distance
action: Keep the one-host rule and state it in the documentation; consider a local regulator in a later revision

effect: Board unusable until traced: after the first rework the source and drain beeped to the host pin while the gate did not
cause: Heat and solder around closely spaced pads with a 0.15 mm annular ring
controls: Re-running the continuity map after each rework
evidence: Aug 2026: second fault after the first rework; how it was resolved is not in the material reviewed
action: Wider pads and ring in Rev B; rework only after re-mapping the legs; record the outcome here

failure_mode: R1 not fitted: Q1's gate is not connected to the host pin
effect: Q1 is never switched, so the SRAM is never power-cycled and every capture returns the same retained state
cause: R1 is the only path from the host gate pin to Q1's gate on this PCB, and the photographed board has it empty
controls: A smoke test of the SRAM supply during a capture
evidence: net check: the host gate net is on J2.8, J1B1.10 and R1.1 only; Q1's gate net is on Q1.2, R1.2 and R2.1 only; photo: R1 pads empty
action: Confirm how the working board was wired (R1 fitted, or a link); mark R1 as required in the schematic

effect: Gate on the wrong leg: the switch never works, or the SRAM is shorted to ground
cause: A TO-92 can be inserted either way; other makers and the BS170 use a different leg order
controls: Check the flat face against the footprint; continuity check
evidence: footprint pin functions S, G, D from the flat face; the BS170 is a different order (to be confirmed in the datasheet)
action: Mark the flat side on the silkscreen; check the datasheet of any substitute part

failure_mode: Header crooked or its plastic melted
effect: Feather does not seat squarely; strain on the pins; contact problems
cause: Heat during soldering; header not held flat
evidence: top-side photo: J1B1 sits crooked with melted plastic at one end
action: Hold headers flat with the Feather fitted as a jig while soldering

failure_mode: The SRAM keeps some power in the off phase
effect: Retained data from the previous state; the start-up pattern is not independent
cause: Current through the input protection diodes with the ground node floating
controls: Measuring the SRAM supply during power-down
evidence: thesis section 3.13.2: on the breadboard prototype the SRAM supply measured under 0.1 V with the gate low; not measured on the shield
action: Repeat the measurement on the shield, with the gate low

effect: More supply noise and dips at SRAM power-up and SPI traffic
cause: C3 left off; only the two 100 nF capacitors are fitted
evidence: photo: C3 pads empty; schematic: C3 is 10 uF across 3V3 and GND
action: Decide whether it is needed; mark do-not-populate if not

failure_mode: Feather inserted the wrong way round
effect: 3V3 and GND on the wrong pins; damage to the Feather or the SRAM
controls: The two header rows have 12 and 16 pins, so only one orientation mates
evidence: J1A1 has 16 pins and J1B1 has 12, matching the Feather's rows
action: Keep the different row lengths; no change needed

failure_mode: 1-wire bus not working (pull-up or header missing)
effect: No temperature readings from the DS18B20
cause: J3 not fitted on the photographed board; R3 is fitted
evidence: photo: J3 empty, R3 fitted; schematic: R3 pulls the bus to 3V3
action: Fit J3 when a probe is attached

cause: Six bottom texts are 0.8 to 0.9 mm high with 0.12 to 0.14 mm lines, under the 1.0 mm and 0.15 mm limits
evidence: measured text settings; the text is legible in the photos
action: Enlarge to 1.0 mm and 0.15 mm in Rev B
